inshape 0.1.0

Structure checks for register microdata.

Register data comes as one row per unit, one row per unit and period (a panel), or one row per spell. Every analysis assumes that shape is right: no duplicated persons, no missing years in the middle of a panel, no person with two addresses at once. inshape checks those assumptions, fast enough for full-population registers, and converts spells to panels.

library(inshape)

persons |>
  ensure_unique(cpr, year, abort_msg = "Duplicate person-years") |>
  ensure_balanced(cpr, year, periods = 2015:2024, gaps_only = TRUE)

addresses |>
  ensure_no_overlap(cpr, start, end)

Installation

inshape is not on CRAN. Install it from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("dataniel/inshape")

Functions

Function Description
add_spell_status() Status from spells on a panel you already have, at primo/ultimo or on a date
describe_changes() Two extracts of a register: keys that came and went, and per column the values that changed, went missing or were filled in
describe_codes() How the codes of a column change over periods: first and last period, codes skipping periods, new and gone codes
describe_key() How well columns work as a key: duplicated keys, exact copies vs. conflicts and the columns they differ in
describe_panel() The structure of a panel: units, gaps, entries and exits per period, participation patterns
describe_spells() Spell data: gaps, transfers (adjacent spells), overlapping, nested and duplicate spells, ongoing and invalid spells
describe_varying() Which columns vary within units: constant, nearly constant (errors) and varying
ensure_balanced() Every unit observed in every period, or no gaps (gaps_only)
ensure_codes() A coded column only holds codes from a code list
ensure_constant() Columns such as sex or birth date are constant within each unit
ensure_no_overlap() Spells (addresses, employment) do not overlap within a unit
ensure_unique() Key columns identify each row uniquely
ensure_within() No rows after death or emigration, or before birth: each row within its unit’s lifetime
merge_spells() Merge spells that follow each other or overlap (transfers, readmissions within max_gap days) into one
spells_to_panel() Spells to a yearly, quarterly or monthly panel with primo and ultimo status

The ensure_*() checkpoints warn or abort with the offending rows and return the data. A failure signals a condition of class inshape_failure that carries the rows.

inshape is made for interactive review of registers. The offending rows of a check are personal data, so inshape writes nothing to disk, neither rows nor a log: a failure shows the count and the first rows at the console, and the rest stay on the condition, in memory. See ?checkpoints.

Built for registers

Character keys such as cpr are compressed to integer ids by a compiled, partitioned and multi-threaded hash, without sorting them; a panel then becomes a bit matrix, one bit per unit and period, read with processor bit instructions; and spell lookups run in one compiled pass over the sorted spells. On 25 million rows (5 million persons over 5 years), describe_panel() takes under 2 seconds. See benchmarks/.

A DuckDB or Arrow table is checked and described in the database, without loading it into R; the describe_*() summaries fetch only their counts:

con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), "register.duckdb")

dplyr::tbl(con, "persons") |>
  ensure_unique(cpr, year) |>
  ensure_balanced(cpr, year, gaps_only = TRUE)

The name

Each Roman census was closed by the inshape, a purification of the people just registered, before the register was accepted. This package is that last step for register data: a registration of the registrations.

Origin

The checks started as expect_unique(), expect_balanced() and expect_no_overlap() in expectr, and the spell conversions in daos. They were renamed to ensure_*() when they moved, so a script using both packages cannot confuse them. expectr keeps the general checkpoints, and the packages do not depend on each other.
